core_idea: New ideas, practices and technologies spread through a social system over time via communication channels. Whether people adopt depends on how they perceive the innovation (relative advantage, compatibility, complexity, trialability, observability). Adopters range from innovators and early adopters to the late majority and laggards, which produces the familiar S-shaped adoption curve.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: Why are some practices, technologies or policies adopted faster than others in a community or organization?
Who adopts first, and through which channels does an innovation spread?
Typical data: surveys on perceived attributes and adoption, interviews with adopters and non-adopters, adoption records over time.
common_mistakes: Assuming the innovation is good and non-adopters are 'resistant' (pro-innovation bias).
Studying only adopters, not rejecters or people who stopped using the innovation.
Treating adopter categories as personality types rather than positions in time.
Ignoring organizational and system context when studying adoption in organizations.
